observations: The role-aware schema validator worked: three distinct normal prefix outcomes were retained without a runner integrity stop.
Zero of three completed prefixes reached effect plus later verification.
One of three completed prefixes produced a confirmed 478-byte patch effect but no later verification, direct evidence that effect-only timing has higher eligibility than H65 timing.
After three ineligible prefixes, six pairs were mathematically impossible; stopping avoided at least four full prefixes and all branches.
All 180,913 consumed model tokens are known; no retry or unknown usage occurred.

cross_round_eligibility.interpretation: Neither observed rate supports expecting six eligible pairs from an unfiltered eight-task cohort.

inference: H65 is too sparse as a general paired benchmark boundary. The next experiment should use a universal observable decision boundary: first confirmed effect when present, otherwise the existing terminal/pressure commitment boundary. Treatment projects the phase-appropriate unresolved reasoning state; control receives the same neutral review.

selected_successor.name: universal decision-bound state
selected_successor.mechanism: Fork at the earliest receipt-confirmed consequential effect, or at terminal/pressure commitment when no effect occurs. Project bounded phase-tagged state only to treatment so every scoreable trajectory can contribute a pair.

alternatives.name: effect-only readiness
alternatives.disposition: retained as the effect branch of H67; insufficient alone at observed prevalence

alternatives.name: terminal compact review
alternatives.disposition: retained as the no-effect branch of H67

open_questions: Can one phase-tagged schema preserve a single treatment while supporting effect and no-effect trajectories?
Can the boundary guarantee eight paired outcomes without adding model tokens before the fork?
Should the next canary require eight complete pairs instead of six because the boundary is universal?
